title: GPT-5 helps solve a 40-year-old problem about Nesterov's accelerated gradient
summary: Ernest Ryu (UCLA) proved why Nesterov's accelerated gradient method, introduced in 1983, remains stable despite the extra momentum that makes it faster. GPT-5's turning point was a rewrite of the equations: not correct as given, but with a structure Ryu then developed and proved himself, over about twelve hours across three days and after a dozen approaches. OpenAI's account says the model created no new mathematical tools and often produced plausible arguments that failed verification.
organization: OpenAI and University of California, Los Angeles

evidence.unknown: OpenAI states GPT-5 often produced plausible but flawed arguments; its restructuring suggestion was not correct as written. The proof was developed and written by Ryu. Whether peer review will confirm it is not reported.
evidence.ai_role: Per OpenAI, GPT-5 suggested approaches and restructured equations; Ryu checked each idea and wrote the final proof. About twelve hours over three days and nearly a dozen approaches. GPT-5 is not a co-author.
